title: Personal Finance explained
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has put strict rules in place to make digital loans safer for you. All online loans must come from banks or Non-Banking Financ.

faq.a: A Regulated Entity (RE) is a financial institution like a bank or a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) that is licensed and supervised by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Under digital lending rules, all loans must ultimately be sanctioned and disbursed by an RE.

faq.q: What is a Key Fact Statement (KFS)?
faq.a: The Key Fact Statement (KFS) is a mandatory, standardised summary document that digital lenders must provide to you before you agree to a loan. It clearly outlines all the essential terms, including the loan amount, tenure, interest rate, all fees and charges, the Annual Percentage Rate (APR), and the cooling-off period.

faq.q: What is the Digital Lending App (DLA) directory?
faq.a: The Digital Lending App (DLA) directory, operationalised by the RBI from July 2025, is a resource where you can check if a digital lending app is linked to an RBI-regulated bank or NBFC. This helps you verify the legitimacy of an app before taking a loan.

faq.q: What if my complaint isn't resolved by the lender?
faq.a: If your complaint with the regulated lender (bank or NBFC) is not resolved to your satisfaction within 30 days, you can escalate the matter to the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS, 2026) through the RBI's Complaint Management System (cms.rbi.org.in).

faq.q: Can I cancel a digital loan after taking it?
faq.a: Yes, the RBI mandates a 'cooling-off period' during which you can exit the digital loan by repaying only the principal amount along with the proportionate Annual Percentage Rate (APR) for the period you held the loan, without incurring any penalties. The minimum period is typically 1 to 3 days, depending on the loan tenure.
